text: SUPERVISOR — new idle-session evidence implicates YOUR live-floor watchdog. The user sat IDLE and the dev log shows heightfield.register for slots 0 and 1 (58564 heightBytes each) firing repeatedly — at least 5 pairs in under a minute, with NO hot update involved — on a ~0.4s rhythm. Your recovery/live-floor.sync logic appears to re-register heightfields EVERY tick instead of only when registration is actually missing. Each re-register ships 58KB over the native bridge (matching the user's rhythmic 10-20ms GC/NATIVE spikes with the time in "other"/bridge) and can re-resolve the ground under the player — prime suspect for the movement rubberband. Print the data: log WHY your sync fires each time (what condition it evaluated); then gate it — re-register ONLY when the floor probe actually shows heightfields missing (post-push recovery), idempotent no-op otherwise; zero register calls during steady idle play is the assertion. Add that as a test/witness check. This outranks the wall-corner work in your queue.
